data.data:
**Skuilder speaks MCP.** An MCP server exposes one course to an agent: cards, data shapes and
their JSON schemas, tags and tag set operations, and navigation strategies, with tools to create,
tag and delete cards and to add strategies.

`npm run studio` writes a `.mcp.json`, so an agent started in your project can work on the course
you have open. Its edits reach your files only when you flush, so they arrive as a reviewable
diff.

[Read: Connect Agents](/vue-skuilder/do/mcp.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**The study loop**: show a card, take a response, update the learner model, choose the next card.

- `StudySession` (Vue, in `@vue-skuilder/common-ui`) renders it.
- `SessionController` (in `@vue-skuilder/db`, no Vue) drives it.
- Each course is a *content source*: asked for cards, it runs its navigation pipeline and returns
  scored candidates.
- The controller keeps two queues: a **supply** queue (new cards and reviews, in rank order) and a
  **failed** queue (cards missed this session, cleared before the session ends).

[Read: The Big Picture](/vue-skuilder/learn/architecture.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**A card type has three parts:**

- a **DataShape**: the schema of its data (named, typed fields);
- a **Question**: a class that grades a response, as correct or not (for scheduling) and how well
  (for ratings, optionally per skill);
- one or more **views**: Vue components that render it.

Each card stores a view ID, `{courseware}.question.{QuestionClass}.{ViewName}`, which is how a
session finds the right class and component.

[Read: Card Data Model](/vue-skuilder/learn/card-data-model.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**A custom card is a Vue component that can do anything**: a game loop, a chess board, a MIDI
keyboard. The platform cares about two moments: the view receives data, and the view submits an
answer.

`useViewable` and `useQuestionView` bridge the two: `submitAnswer(answer)` grades the answer with
your `Question` class and hands the record to the session. Register question classes in a
`CourseWare`, and add it to `allCourseWare`.

For a widget inside otherwise-markdown cards, an inline component is lighter.

[Read: Creating Custom Cards](/vue-skuilder/extend/custom-cards.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**Everything reads and writes through data-layer interfaces** (`UserDBInterface`,
`CourseDBInterface`, ...), with two implementations:

- **couch**: CouchDB on the server, PouchDB in the browser. Accounts, sync, live card ratings,
  classrooms. A course can opt in to a local replica for fast reads.
- **static**: course content packed as JSON and served from any host; learner data in the browser
  with no sync; card ratings frozen at pack time.

Navigation strategies are documents in the course, so a static course runs the same pipeline as a
live one. This course is a static one.

[Read: Data Layer](/vue-skuilder/learn/data-layer.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**How the next card is chosen.** Every plan runs the course's pipeline:

`Generate → Filter → Drop zeros → Regulate → Hints → Diversity re-rank → Select`

- **Generators** propose candidates: new cards near your rating, due reviews, authored targets.
- **Filters** multiply scores. A *gate* says "not ready yet"; a *signal* expresses preference.
- **Regulators** balance reviews against new material.

Every card carries **provenance**: what each stage did to its score, and why. Ratings are kept
globally and per skill (tag), and practice leans toward your weakest skills.

[Read: Pedagogy](/vue-skuilder/learn/pedagogy.html)

**This is a skuilder study session**, running inside the docs site.

The course is static JSON served with these pages. Your answers, ratings and review schedule are
kept in this browser, and nothing is sent anywhere.

Questions about a docs page unlock once you've read that page, or once you've met its
introduction card here. Read a page, come back, and its questions are in play.

data.name: Input
data.data:
**Extending the pipeline.** Write a generator (`getWeightedCards`) or a filter (`transform`),
register it at app start with `registerNavigator(name, Class, role)`, and enable it for a course
with a strategy document naming it.

Filters multiply scores, so their order doesn't matter, and a 0 excludes a card. A filter and the
app can share state through a strategy-state document.

*This course does exactly that.* The docs site registers a filter that reads which pages you've
read, from strategy state, and holds back questions on pages you haven't.

[Read: Navigation Strategies](/vue-skuilder/extend/navigation-strategies.html)

data.name: Input
data.data:
**The static-course workflow:**

1. `npx @vue-skuilder/cli init mycourse --data-layer static`: a standalone app for one course.
2. `npm run studio`: a scratch CouchDB, an editor, and an MCP server, on your machine.
3. **Flush** in the editor: the course is written back to your project's static files.
4. Commit, `npm run build`, deploy anywhere static.

Custom card types in `src/questions/` are built into the studio editor too. For many courses
with shared accounts, there is `platform-ui` with the `express` backend.

[Read: Quickstart](/vue-skuilder/do/quickstart.html)
